rachel (support): BeaconHealth reporting intermittent TLS failures in their private VPC after our cert rotation this morning. Java 8 clients get 'tls: bad certificate' and mobile clients sometimes fallback to HTTP/1.1 with 502s. Can we confirm what rotator deployed?

cert-rotator-bot: rotation completed for tenant beaconhealth at 2026-03-15T09:12:08Z. Deployed leaf cert CN=api.beaconhealth.internal, sig alg: ECDSA-with-SHA256, chain length 3.

mike (eng-infra): looking. Any quick repro steps from the customer?

rachel (support): Customer sent these steps they used from inside their VPC: `openssl s_client -connect api.beaconhealth.internal:443 -servername api.beaconhealth.internal -showcerts` output attached (excerpt):
```
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.beaconhealth.internal
   i:/CN=Redwood Interm RSA 2024
 1 s:/CN=Redwood Interm RSA 2024
   i:/CN=Redwood Root CA
```
ServerKeyExchange uses ECDSA
verify return:1\n```
They also ran a Java client and got: `javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: sun.security.validator.ValidatorException: PKIX path building failed`\n\nsandeep (eng-runtime): hmm. rotator bot said deployed ECDSA leaf, but openssl shows intermediate named 'Redwood Interm RSA 2024' — that's an RSA-signed intermediate. Could be a cross-signed chain where leaf uses ECDSA key but chain contains an RSA intermediate. Java 8 stacks sometimes reject chains where signature algorithms or key types change unexpectedly.

mike (eng-infra): also check HAProxy / LB cipher priorities in their VPC. If the LB prefers ECDSA ciphers and the client only supports RSA, the handshake could fail early. But error message is PKIX path building failed (client couldn't validate chain), which is different.

jessica (customer-success): I confirmed BeaconHealth runs an older internal truststore pinned to a fingerprint of the intermediate they cached last year (fingerprint matches previous 'Redwood Interm ECDSA 2022'). They did not update pin after migration.

rachel (support): so 2 simultaneous factors: (1) customer truststore pinned to old intermediate fingerprint, (2) leaf now uses ECDSA key and our rotator served a chain that does not include the old intermediate. That would cause PKIX failures.

sandeep (eng-runtime): Agreed. Repro matrix:
- If client truststore contains only old ECDSA-intermediate fingerprint => validation fails when presented RSA-intermediate.
- If client supports ECDSA but server negotiates RSA (depends on LB ciphers) => could fall back but chain mismatch still breaks.

mike (eng-infra): Quick mitigation options:
1) Re-issue a chain that includes the old ECDSA intermediate (cross-signed) so pinned clients see the fingerprint they expect.
2) Ask customer to update pinned fingerprint/truststore (longer lead).
3) On our side, rotator could serve both chains via SNI variation, but that is more invasive.

rachel (support): BeaconHealth asked for immediate workaround to stop 502s for their users. Which is fastest?

sandeep (eng-runtime): Short-term: redeploy a compatibility chain that includes the previously pinned intermediate (option 1). I can generate a chain using the cross-signed ECDSA intermediate we keep for compat. Will need a signed bundle upload and a quick restart of the private endpoint probe (no downtime for hosted clients).

mike (eng-infra): I'll coordinate the bundle upload with the rotator. Note: need to confirm the exact fingerprint BeaconHealth pinned. Jessica, can you get the fingerprint hex from the customer?

jessica (customer-success): Sent them a quick script to run: `openssl x509 -in interm.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256`. They returned: `SHA256 Fingerprint=AB:12:34:56:78:9C:...` (truncated in slack, full one in ticket).

mike (eng-infra): Got it. We'll assemble a chain that includes the matching intermediate and push. ETA ~20m.

cert-rotator-bot: deploying compatibility bundle for tenant beaconhealth (bundle-id cb-20260315-9).

rachel (support): Customer confirmed: after ~15m they see fewer errors. Mobile still had a handful of 502s but desktop flows cleared.

sandeep (eng-runtime): Action items:
- Short: keep compatibility chain for 72h while customer updates truststore (owner: sandeep).
- Mid: add a compatibility matrix note to rotator doc about cross-signed intermediates and ECDSA/RSA leaf combos (owner: mike).
- Long: consider rotator support for dual-chain serving or offering a 'compatibility bundle' option in private deployments (owner: product).

mike (eng-infra): Also adding a health-check probe to detect when customer's pinned fingerprint mismatches and automatically notify CS. Could be helpful.

jessica (customer-success): BeaconHealth will schedule an internal rollout to update truststores. They appreciate the fast workaround.

rachel (support): closing loop: please add notes to the support ticket and mark incident as 'mitigated' once compatibility chain is in place. :white_check_mark:

sandeep (eng-runtime): added notes to ticket, leaving compatibility chain in place. Will remove after confirmation from CS.

mike (eng-infra): follow-up: created PR to rotator docs with recommendations (PR #512).

jessica (customer-success): customer confirmed full recovery 2026-03-15T09:42:00Z. Thanks team! :tada!
